methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update a session.

 @internal
 The authorization and state-operation are determined depending on whether the session
 is going to be created or updated which is determined as part of the request execution.

methods.name: UpdateSubject
methods.description:
Set the session subject.

 This is a targeted update that modifies only the subject field,
 leaving other session fields untouched. Use this instead of the full
 update RPC when you only need to change the session subject.

 @internal
 Server-side field-level update, race-safe. Atomically modifies only
 spec.subject without touching other fields.

methods.name: UpdateSessionMemory
methods.description:
Persist session memory after execution.

 Atomically updates only status.session_memory, leaving all other
 session fields untouched. Called by the cursor-runner after each
 completed execution turn.

 @internal
 Server-side field-level update, race-safe. No full-document replace.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a session.

 @internal
 Restricted to platform operators to preserve the billing and audit trail.
 Regular users (including session owners) cannot delete sessions.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines whether
 users outside that organization can access the resource.

 The three visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#member tuple (all org members)
 - PUBLIC: resource#viewer@identity_account:* with allow_public (all users)

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner (and explicitly granted principals) can access.
 This is the default for instances and personal resources.
 Named visibility_private to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Anyone can access (read) this resource.
 Used for marketplace-published resources (e.g., "stigmer/web-search").
 Write access still requires org membership.
 Named visibility_public to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
All members of the owning organization can access (read) this resource.
 Used for instances where a team wants shared observability of executions
 without granting access to all authenticated users.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#member

 For workflow instances, this enables zero-tuple-per-execution shared
 observability: all org members see all executions via inheritance.

enumTypes.name: Harness
enumTypes.description:
Harness identifies the execution engine that processes agent activities
 for a session.

 Each harness corresponds to a different Temporal activity type registered
 by the runner daemon. The harness determines:
 - Which tools the agent has access to
 - How conversation state is managed (Stigmer checkpoints vs engine-native)
 - Which LLM models are available
 - Billing tier and cost structure

 HARNESS_UNSPECIFIED defaults to HARNESS_NATIVE for backward compatibility.

values.name: HARNESS_NATIVE
values.description:
Stigmer's native execution engine.

 Stigmer-managed checkpoints, custom tools, sandbox isolation,
 pause/resume, and full HITL approval flow.

values.name: HARNESS_CURSOR
values.description:
Cursor SDK execution engine.

 Cursor-managed conversation state, Cursor built-in tools + MCP,
 both local and cloud runtimes. Premium billing tier.

enumTypes.name: CursorMode
enumTypes.description:
CursorMode selects the Cursor SDK agent type for sessions using
 HARNESS_CURSOR.

 Determined once at session creation based on workspace entries and never
 changed mid-session. Switching would lose Cursor-side conversation state
 because local agents (agent- prefix) and cloud agents (bc- prefix) maintain
 separate, incompatible conversation stores.

 Ignored when harness is not HARNESS_CURSOR.

 @internal
 Mode selection logic (when feature flag STIGMER_CURSOR_CLOUD_MODE_ENABLED
 is true):
   - All workspace entries are GitRepoSource -> CURSOR_MODE_CLOUD
   - Any workspace entry is LocalPathSource  -> CURSOR_MODE_LOCAL
   - Feature flag disabled                   -> CURSOR_MODE_LOCAL (forced)

 When UNSPECIFIED on an existing session, the runner treats it as LOCAL
 for backward compatibility with sessions created before this field existed.

values.name: CURSOR_MODE_LOCAL
values.description:
Local Cursor agent created with a local cwd configuration.

 Works with any workspace source (git or local path). Stigmer owns
 the durable conversation layer — always sends continuation prompts
 because Cursor local agents do not reliably retain context across
 Agent.send() calls.

values.name: CURSOR_MODE_CLOUD
values.description:
Cloud Cursor agent created with a cloud repos configuration.

 Requires all workspace entries to be GitRepoSource (HTTPS URLs).
 Cursor natively manages conversation state for cloud agents, but
 Stigmer persists session memory as backup because cloud agents can
 expire. Feature-flagged — requires STIGMER_CURSOR_CLOUD_MODE_ENABLED.

enumTypes.name: ExecutionTarget
enumTypes.description:
ExecutionTarget specifies where session activities are executed.

 Determines whether the runner that processes agent activities lives on the
 client's machine (desktop app or CLI) or in a cloud-provisioned sandbox.
 Set at session creation time and immutable once an execution has run —
 workspace state may not be portable between local and cloud environments.

 @internal
 The control plane uses this field in dispatch to decide whether to route
 activities to a client-polled per-session queue (LOCAL) or provision a
 cloud sandbox (CLOUD). Both use task queues named "session:{session_id}".
 The difference is who provides the runner: the client (LOCAL) or the
 server (CLOUD).

values.name: EXECUTION_TARGET_LOCAL
values.description:
Client's embedded runner handles activities.

 Desktop app or CLI spawns a local runner process that polls the
 session's task queue. No server-side provisioning needed.

values.name: EXECUTION_TARGET_CLOUD
values.description:
Server provisions a cloud sandbox for execution.

 The control plane triggers EnsureSessionSandbox to create an isolated
 environment with a runner polling the session's task queue.

enumTypes.name: GitWriteBackMode
enumTypes.description:
GitWriteBackMode controls the platform's git workflow for a git-backed workspace entry.

 @internal
 The platform enables write-back by default when credentials are
 available. Users can override this per-session by setting an
 explicit mode. The agent never sees or controls this setting.

values.name: GIT_WRITE_BACK_BRANCH_AND_PR
values.description:
Create a branch and pull request from the agent's file changes after execution completes.

 @internal
 The platform automatically detects uncommitted changes via git diff,
 creates a branch (stigmer/{execution_id_short}), commits all changes,
 pushes the branch to the remote, and creates a pull request targeting
 the original branch. The write-back outcome is recorded in
 AgentExecutionStatus.workspace_write_backs.

resourceDescription: Session represents a multi-turn conversation thread with an agent.

statusType.name: SessionStatus
statusType.description:
SessionStatus contains system-managed runtime state for a session.

 This follows the same pattern as AgentExecutionStatus: domain-specific
 status fields alongside the standard audit at field 99.

 Previously Session.status was ApiResourceAuditStatus (audit-only). The
 introduction of session memory required a proper status message. The
 wire format is backward-compatible: ApiResourceAuditStatus.audit was at
 field 99, and SessionStatus.audit is at the same field number, so
 existing MongoDB documents deserialize correctly.

fields.name: SessionMemory
fields.description:
Durable session memory for continuation across agent evictions.

 Updated after each completed execution turn by the runner. When a
 fresh agent is created (because the previous one expired or the local
 store lookup failed), the continuation prompt is built from this
 memory.

 Empty until the first execution completes. Never cleared — only
 overwritten with newer state.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

fields.name: Avatar

fields.name: CreatedBy

fields.name: CreatedAt

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: ConversationTurn
statusNestedTypes.description:
ConversationTurn captures a single message in the conversation for replay.

 Used in the continuation prompt to give the fresh agent recent context.
 Content may be truncated if the original message exceeded the per-turn
 token limit.

fields.name: Role
fields.description:
The role of the message author.
 Values: "user" or "assistant"

fields.name: Content
fields.description:
The message content, potentially truncated.

 If the original message exceeded 1k tokens, this contains the last
 1k tokens prefixed with "[truncated]".

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the message was sent.
 Example: "2026-05-09T15:30:00Z"

 Uses string (not google.protobuf.Timestamp) for consistency with
 AgentMessage.timestamp and other operational timestamps in this domain.

statusNestedTypes.name: SessionMemory
statusNestedTypes.description:
SessionMemory captures durable conversation state that survives agent
 eviction, process restarts, and Cursor SDK "agent not found" failures.

 Updated after each completed execution turn and stored in SessionStatus.
 When a fresh agent is created (because the previous one expired or the
 local store lookup failed), the continuation prompt is built from this
 memory — giving the new agent the full context of the prior conversation.

 Design: Structured extraction, not LLM summarization. The cursor-runner
 parses stream events (tool calls, file edits, command outputs) and
 populates these fields directly. No separate LLM call is made in v1.

 Token budgets (enforced at persist-time by the runner):
   durable_summary:    max 2k tokens
   recent_turns:       max 4k tokens (last 6 turns, FIFO)
   tool_observations:  max 1k tokens (most recent, FIFO)
   Total continuation prompt ceiling: 8k tokens

 @internal
 Persisted in MongoDB as part of the Session document under status.
 The runner reads it from the activity input (passed by the workflow)
 and writes it back via gRPC after each completed turn.

fields.name: DurableSummary
fields.description:
High-level narrative of what has been accomplished so far.

 Includes the original goal, current progress, and next steps.
 Built by the runner from assistant messages — not a verbatim transcript.

 Token budget: max 2k tokens. Truncated at persist-time if exceeded.

fields.name: WorkspaceDigest
fields.description:
Digest of the workspace state at the time of last persistence.

 Free-form string capturing relevant workspace context (e.g., git branch,
 HEAD SHA, working directory). Used by the continuation prompt to help
 the fresh agent orient itself.

fields.name: ChangedFiles
fields.description:
Files created or modified during the session.

 Extracted from tool-call events (file_edit, file_create, etc.).
 Helps the continuation prompt tell the fresh agent what has changed.

fields.name: OpenTasks
fields.description:
Outstanding tasks or questions the agent identified but has not completed.

 Parsed from the agent's final message or todo-list tool calls.
 Gives the continuation prompt a "pick up where you left off" list.

fields.name: ToolObservations
fields.description:
Summaries of significant tool executions during the session.

 Captures command, working directory, exit code, and a short output summary.
 Most recent observations first, FIFO-pruned to ~10 entries.

 Token budget: max 1k tokens total across all observations.

fields.name: RecentTurns
fields.description:
Recent conversation turns for verbatim replay in the continuation prompt.

 Last 6 turns (3 user + 3 assistant), FIFO. Individual turns exceeding
 1k tokens are truncated to the last 1k tokens with a "[truncated]" prefix.

 Token budget: max 4k tokens total across all turns.

fields.name: Decisions
fields.description:
Explicit decisions the agent made during the session.

 Extracted from assistant messages where the agent explains a choice
 (e.g., "chose library X over Y because..."). Append-only, never pruned,
 capped at 20 entries.

 These survive summary regeneration — even if durable_summary is
 rewritten, the individual decision records are preserved.

fields.name: FailedAttempts
fields.description:
Approaches that were tried and failed during the session.

 Extracted from tool failures, error recoveries, and explicit agent
 statements about abandoned approaches. Append-only, never pruned,
 capped at 20 entries.

 Prevents the continuation agent from repeating mistakes the previous
 agent already learned from.

statusNestedTypes.name: ToolObservation
statusNestedTypes.description:
ToolObservation captures the outcome of a significant tool execution.

 Not every tool call produces an observation — only commands with meaningful
 output (shell commands, file operations with errors, etc.) are recorded.
 The runner decides which tool calls are "significant" based on tool type
 and outcome.

fields.name: Command
fields.description:
The command or tool invocation that was executed.
 Example: "npm install", "git checkout -b feature/foo"

fields.name: Cwd
fields.description:
Working directory where the command was executed.
 Example: "/workspace/stigmer"

fields.name: ExitCode
fields.description:
Process exit code (0 = success).
 Meaningful for shell commands; may be 0 for non-shell tools.

fields.name: Summary
fields.description:
Short summary of the tool output.

 Not the full stdout/stderr — a concise description of what happened.
 Example: "Installed 42 packages, 0 vulnerabilities"
 Example: "Command failed: permission denied on /etc/hosts"
